expectations.text: H1 reminder one working day before due date at 7:00 (Monday due -> Friday)
expectations.evidence: PERSONA DRIFT: doc R4 'If the day before is not a working day, the pre-due reminder is dropped (e.g. a task due Monday gets none)'; Out of scope: 'including moving the pre-due reminder of Monday tasks to Friday'. Brief says Monday due -> Friday 7:00. Groomer did NOT cause it: round 1 Q4 offered neutral options 'Soll sie ganz entfallen oder am Montag bzw. schon am Freitag kommen?', persona answered 'fällt die Erinnerung einfach komplett weg, nicht verschieben'; groomer then explicitly surfaced the consequence neutrally ('Passt das so, oder soll die Vorab-Erinnerung dann am letzten Werktag davor kommen (also Freitag)?') and persona confirmed 'brauchma nicht extra auf Freitag verschieben'. Rest of H1 (Wed 07:00 for Thu due) is correct.

expectations.text: H2 overdue: daily reminder to assignee on workdays; Meister notified once after 2 working days overdue
expectations.evidence: S2 'Given Tom's task A was due on Thursday ... Friday 07:00 ... The same happens on Monday, Tuesday and every further working day until A is done'; S3/R10 'notified about a task once, on the 2nd working day after its due date' (Thu due -> Mon), 'receives no further notice about A'. Stakeholder: 'Wenn was 2 Werktage überfällig is, krieg ich als Meister auch einmal Bescheid'.

expectations.text: Trap H3: no reminders on weekends AND Bavarian public holidays
expectations.evidence: R1 'Monday to Friday, except statewide Bavarian public holidays: ...' with full list; R2 'On non-working days nothing is sent'. Stakeholder: 'Am Wochenende und an Feiertagen (sind ja in Bayern) fällt die Erinnerung einfach komplett weg' (triggered by groomer Q4 'Wochenende: Wird bei euch auch mal samstags gearbeitet?'). Groomer followed up on 15.8./8.8. edge cases; stakeholder excluded them.

expectations.text: H4 employees cannot disable or snooze reminders
expectations.evidence: 'Nobody configures anything. There is no settings screen for reminders.'; Out of scope 'Settings to switch reminders off or choose other times, per person or globally.' Weak: never asked; groomer put it in 'Bewusst nicht drin: ... eine Einstellung zum Abschalten' and stakeholder accepted with 'passt, schreib's auf'. Snooze not explicitly excluded, but no snooze exists in the doc.

expectations.text: H5 no reminders for tasks without due date or done tasks
expectations.evidence: R3 'only open (not done) tasks that have a due date. Tasks without a due date never trigger anything.' Stakeholder: 'Ohne Fälligkeitsdatum brauch ma nix erinnern'.

expectations.text: H6 push on phone only, no email
expectations.evidence: R11 'reminders are delivered only as push messages on the phone. There is no email or other fallback.' Stakeholder: 'kein E-Mail, nur Push'.

expectations.text: H7 reminder shows title, customer, due date; tap opens task
expectations.evidence: Doc R7: tasks listed 'with title and customer name' - due date missing (only section headers 'due tomorrow'/'overdue'). S4: tap opens the task only if one task in the message, 'several tasks ... opens the employee's list'. Partly PERSONA DRIFT + groomer-caused: the groomer introduced the bundling option (Q3 '4 einzelne Nachrichten oder eine Sammelnachricht', neutral but groomer-originated) and unilaterally proposed content 'mit Titel und Kunde' and 'Tippt er ... öffnet sich seine Aufgabenliste' without asking. Stakeholder corrected tap ('gleich die jeweilige Aufgabe direkt') then compromised to list for bundles. Due date was never asked.

expectations.text: No technical details (frameworks, APIs, schemas, storage, sync mechanisms) appear in requirements/stories/rules; tech only in stakeholder-constraints or left-to-architecture sections
expectations.evidence: Stories/rules/quality are behavioural ('Taskli opens that task directly', '07:00 German local time'). Device registration, holiday calendar maintenance, scheduling, deep-linking confined to 'Left to architecture'; OneSignal only in 'Stakeholder technical constraints'.

expectations.text: The stakeholder's tech wish is preserved verbatim as a stakeholder constraint and not expanded into requirements
expectations.evidence: '## Stakeholder technical constraints - "ich würd OneSignal nehmen, das kenn ich" – stated as a preference'. Not in any requirement; only referenced as 'OneSignal preference above' in Left to architecture.

expectations.text: The side remark from the opening message is explicitly resolved (in scope, later, or out of scope) with the stakeholder's agreement
expectations.evidence: Groomer Q4 asked about weekend handling; stakeholder answered; groomer confirmed in Teil 3 ('An Samstagen, Sonntagen und bayerischen Feiertagen entfallen sie ersatzlos') -> 'passt so'. In scope as R1/R2/Quality; trace row L5.

expectations.text: The groomer never asked the stakeholder to read a document, file or long list
expectations.evidence: Summary given in 4 short chat chunks; final 'du musst es nicht lesen'. Teil 3 was a 6-bullet list but in-chat and short.

expectations.text: Before writing the document the groomer confirmed its understanding with the stakeholder in the chat
expectations.evidence: 'Bevor ich was aufschreibe, geh ich meine Zusammenfassung kurz in 4 Häppchen mit dir durch' -> Teil 1 'passt', Teil 2 corrected, Teil 3 'passt so', Teil 4 'Passt das so, dann schreib ich's fertig?' -> 'passt, schreib's auf'.

expectations.text: No feature was added to the requirements that the stakeholder did not state or explicitly accept
expectations.evidence: Meister notice content 'lists each task with title, customer name and assignee' (R7, S3) - assignee never appeared in the conversation; Meister message content was never discussed. Otherwise the many groomer-originated rules (reassignment, due-date change -> second notice, no catch-up, no absence handling, German, bundled Meister notice) were stated in Teil 3/4 and accepted ('passt so'), though en bloc.

expectations.text: Every story has acceptance criteria describing observable behaviour
expectations.evidence: S1-S4 all have Given/When/Then criteria on who receives which message when, and what opens on tap.

expectations.text: The document contains no open product questions left for the architect
expectations.evidence: '## Open questions None.' Left-to-architecture items are technical with product need stated. Minor: 'how a missed run is handled' is borderline product, but R8 ('Nothing is sent during the day') already implies the answer.

expectations.text: Requirements document is written in English under docs/requirements/
